summary: Sporting News's Week 14 PPR running back rankings, written for the final week of the fantasy football regular season, cover start/sit advice, sleepers, busts and injuries. Christian McCaffrey tops the list, followed by Austin Ekeler and Travis Etienne Jr. Only the Commanders and Cardinals are on bye, and the piece includes a full ranking of 63 RBs.
one_line: Sporting News ranks 63 running backs for Week 14 PPR fantasy football, with sleepers, busts, bye weeks and injury updates.
key_facts: Only the Commanders and Cardinals are on bye in Week 14, taking Brian Robinson Jr. and James Conner off the table; six teams were on bye in Week 13.
Christian McCaffrey (49ers vs. Seahawks) is ranked No. 1 and Austin Ekeler (Chargers vs. Broncos) is No. 2 in the Week 14 PPR RB rankings.
Austin Ekeler has averaged fewer than 3.0 yards per carry since coming off IR eight games ago, but the Broncos have surrendered the most PPR points in the NFL to RBs.
Travis Etienne Jr. (Jaguars @ Browns) averaged 17.4 PPR points per game entering Week 13, third best in the NFL.
De'Von Achane returned in Week 13 from a knee injury with 103 yards and two TDs on the Commanders, and averages 20.6 PPR points per game, third in the NFL; he and Raheem Mostert are ranked 4 and 5.
Tyjae Spears (Titans @ Dolphins) averaged 5.1 yards per carry entering Week 13 and is a sleeper if Derrick Henry (head/neck) is out; Will Levis is the Titans' rookie QB.
Keaton Mitchell (Ravens vs. Rams) has over 300 yards and two TDs over the Ravens' past four games and can run 22 miles per hour.
Najee Harris (Steelers vs. Patriots) is a high-ceiling RB2 in a Thursday night game, with Kenny Pickett (ankle) out.
James Cook (Bills @ Chiefs), Zach Charbonnet (Seahawks @ 49ers) and Tyler Allgeier (Falcons vs. Buccaneers) are named as potential busts; Allgeier averaged nine touches over the past two weeks.
Rhamondre Stevenson (ankle) will be out, so Ezekiel Elliott (Patriots @ Steelers) could see 20 touches.
Jonathan Taylor (thumb) had surgery last week and will miss the next few weeks, opening the door for Zack Moss as the Colts' lead back.
Washington and Arizona both rank among the 10 most generous teams to RBs this season; the Panthers allowed 28.9 FPPG to RBs entering Week 13.
